take_homes: Do not make many agents when one is enough. Only split if the work needs different access.
When work passes from one agent to the next, numbers get lost. Check the handoff.
The agent can suggest and a person presses go. That is the safe way, and the question 'what could it do with this access' is a good one.

monday.stop_condition: If someone shows me an agent that builds the weekly depot delivery report from a real file, I would try it.
monday.blocker: No time. The reporting is in a system I cannot export from without IT. Examples were Confluence and strategy, not logistics.

misconception.why: Nothing here was about operations or customers. The one exception was the Slack demo, which showed an agent doing something outside a chat window. It was not enough to change my mind that AI is for operations.

one_line: Too much English and too many fancy words. I got that you should not split agents without a reason, and that nobody checks if the answer is true. Show me my own shift plan next time.
